name: blood

attributes.attribute: a mythic theme among the Celts
said by Romans to be sacred to the Celts
smeared on trees in sacred groves as sacrifice
seen as carrying the essence or life force

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Blood is a mythic theme among the Celts. Roman writers called it sacred to them. They told of drinking slain enemies' blood. Their claims need a skeptical eye. Their audience feared the Celts. Those warriors nearly conquered Rome. Roman authors may paint the Celts as bloodthirsty. Yet other signs support blood rituals. Blood brotherhood lasted in the Scottish isles into recent times. Animal sacrifice blood was smeared on sacred grove trees. Blood was seen as carrying the essence, or life force. Drinking it would restore the warrior.

okr.objective: Describe blood as a sacred substance and the rituals around it.
key_results: Roman writers called blood sacred to the Celts.
Roman claims about bloodthirst are viewed with suspicion.
Blood brotherhood survived in the Scottish isles.
Sacrificial blood was smeared on sacred grove trees.
